justification: Site A is fully and correctly identified: the unguarded dereference at FileTxnLog.java:380-381, with the exact chain that leaves inputStream null (no log.* file in the txnlog dir -> FileTxnIterator.init leaves storedFiles empty -> goToNextLog()'s 'if (storedFiles.size() > 0)' is false -> createInputArchive(), the only assignment of inputStream, is never called). Enumerates three distinct branch conditions that empty the iterator (no log files at all; an empty/preallocated first log file; fast-forward exhausting every txn) and identifies the missing guard. Mentions Observer.observeLeader only as a stack frame, never its catch clause; the repetition is credited to QuorumPeer.run:961's broad catch. Site B is absent. The run never mentions Observer.java:85, the 'catch (IOException e)' in Observer.observeLeader, or the fact that the NullPointerException is a RuntimeException the handler does not match. It attributes the repetition to QuorumPeer.run's broad 'catch (Exception e)' at 962-963 instead. That attribution is itself correct - the peer would re-enter OBSERVING even with a widened handler - but QuorumPeer.run is not a line the fix changed, and the run says nothing about the exception bypassing the observer's own handler. Under the pre-registered rule (both sites required; METHODOLOGY §10 requires every site the fix touched and §8 forbids partial credit) this is a FAIL.
